accepted.s: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by which Ministry of the Government of India?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
accepted.x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
accepted.tq: Identify the ministry associated with the legislation rather than its implementing agencies.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, which one of the following is correct regarding the definition of a child?
o: A person below 16 years, only if female
A person below 14 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 21 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 18 years, irrespective of gender
accepted.x: POCSO treats every person below 18 years as a child and applies in a gender-neutral manner.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the age and gender-neutral definition under POCSO from other child-related laws.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: Under the POCSO Act, an offence committed by a person in a position of trust is treated as
o: an offence applicable only to institutions
accepted.x: The Act treats offences committed by a person in a position of trust as aggravated offences.
accepted.tq: Test the legal consequence attached to a special relationship of trust.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the special courts constituted under the POCSO Act?
o: They permit publication of the victim's identity after filing of the charge-sheet
They conduct trials only in public hearings
They transfer every case to a Children's Court
They provide child-friendly trials and keep the victim's identity secret
accepted.x: POCSO special courts are intended to conduct child-friendly trials and protect the identity of the victim.
accepted.tq: Select the option combining the two safeguards specifically associated with special courts.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the POCSO Act:
1. Section 19 deals with mandatory reporting of offences.
2. Sections 29 and 30 provide for presumptions against the accused.
3. The investigation is required to be completed within two months and the trial within one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting; Sections 29 and 30 contain presumptions against the accused; and the prescribed timelines are two months for investigation and one year for trial.
accepted.tq: Link section numbers with their subjects and check the statutory timelines together.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: The 21 April 2018 Ordinance relating to the POCSO Act primarily provided for
o: replacement of mandatory reporting with voluntary reporting
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
lowering the age of a child to 14 years
accepted.x: The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
accepted.tq: Match the dated legislative measure with its principal substantive change.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: It introduced the death penalty for aggravated penetrative assault and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years
It removed the punishment of imprisonment for aggravated penetrative assault
It made all POCSO offences compoundable
It reduced the minimum punishment to 7 years
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment provided for the death penalty in aggravated penetrative assault cases and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years. The POCSO Rules were framed in 2020.
accepted.tq: Use the precise punishment figures to distinguish the amendment from neighbouring provisions.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: The POCSO Rules associated with the 2019 amendment were framed in
accepted.x: The POCSO Rules were framed in 2020 following the 2019 amendment.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of amendment from the subsequent year of rules formulation.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s:
With reference to the age of consent under POCSO, consider the following statements:
1. The Standing Committee on Home Affairs, in its 167th Report of 2012, supported retaining 18 years.
2. The Law Commission, in its 283rd Report of 2023, stated that lowering the age could make POCSO a “paper law”.
3. The Supreme Court in January 2026 urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause for consensual adolescent relationships.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 2012 Standing Committee supported 18 years, the 2023 Law Commission warned against lowering it, and the Supreme Court suggested a Romeo-Juliet clause in January 2026.
accepted.tq: Arrange the reports and judicial development by institution and year before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: The Supreme Court's January 2026 suggestion concerning consensual adolescent relationships was described as a
accepted.x: The Supreme Court suggested consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause for consensual adolescent relationships.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar policy expressions by recalling the exact judicial phrase.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full name, enforcement, amendments, age definition, standing committee view

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015?
o: Child in Need of Care and Protection — Juvenile Justice Board
Child in Conflict with Law — Child Welfare Committee
Child in Need of Care and Protection — Child Welfare Committee
Child in Conflict with Law — District Magistrate alone
accepted.x: A Child in Need of Care and Protection is dealt with by the Child Welfare Committee, while a Child in Conflict with Law is dealt with by the Juvenile Justice Board.
accepted.tq: Start with the institutional pair and distinguish the two statutory child categories.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Juvenile Justice Boards and Child Welfare Committees:
1. Every district has both a Juvenile Justice Board and a Child Welfare Committee.
2. Each of them must have at least one woman member.
3. Children in Conflict with Law are dealt with by Child Welfare Committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Every district has both bodies and each must include at least one woman member. Statement 3 is false because Children in Conflict with Law are dealt with by Juvenile Justice Boards.
accepted.tq: Find the institutional mismatch in the third statement while retaining the composition facts.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s: A child aged 17 years is alleged to have committed a heinous offence carrying a minimum punishment of seven years. Under the Juvenile Justice Act, the first statutory step is generally
o: discharge by the Child Welfare Committee
preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board
trial directly by the High Court
automatic transfer to an adult prison
accepted.x: For a child in the 16–18 age group accused of a heinous offence carrying a minimum punishment of seven years, the Juvenile Justice Board conducts a preliminary assessment. The matter may thereafter be transferred to the Children's Court.
accepted.tq: Apply the age-plus-offence threshold before considering possible transfer to a Children's Court.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the procedure applicable to a 16–18-year-old accused of a heinous offence under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015?
o: Children's Court trial followed by JJB preliminary assessment
JJB preliminary assessment followed, where appropriate, by transfer to the Children's Court
Child Welfare Committee inquiry followed by automatic adult trial
District Magistrate inquiry followed by transfer to the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The Juvenile Justice Board conducts the preliminary assessment first; a possible subsequent transfer is to the Children's Court.
accepted.tq: Test procedural order by identifying the first statutory authority and the possible later authority.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s: The guiding principle in dealing with juvenile offenders through juvenile courts or Juvenile Justice Boards is
o: the best interests of the child
accepted.x: Juvenile offenders are dealt with under the guiding principle of the best interests of the child.
accepted.tq: Identify the governing principle rather than the procedural body.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s: The 2021 amendment to the Juvenile Justice framework strengthened the role of the
o: Gram Panchayat, including in criminal sentencing
Election Commission, including in adoption orders
District Magistrate, including in adoption orders
Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, including in custody orders
accepted.x: The 2021 amendment strengthened the role of District Magistrates, including their role in adoption orders.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-function pair to avoid swapping the District Magistrate with another institution.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Juvenile Justice Boards are headed by a
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, Juvenile Justice Boards are headed by a female Principal Magistrate.
accepted.tq: Test the specific Andhra Pradesh institutional arrangement rather than the general national structure.
accepted.sec: Juvenile Justice Act 2015 - JJBs, children's courts, CWCs, 16-18 age group, AP procedures

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported Child Welfare Committee figures for Andhra Pradesh in 2025–26?
o: 55 cases and 4,189 children declared free for adoption
4,189 cases and 55 children declared free for adoption
418 cases and 55 children declared free for adoption
4,189 cases and 550 children declared free for adoption
accepted.x: The reported Andhra Pradesh figures for 2025–26 were 4,189 cases handled and 55 children declared free for adoption.
accepted.tq: Separate the case total from the smaller adoption-related count.

accepted.x: Boards are being set up for the 13 new districts in Andhra Pradesh.

accepted.s: The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) became a statutory body under the
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
accepted.x: CARA became a statutory body under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory body with its parent legislation, not with the subject matter alone.

accepted.s: Under the Adoption Regulations, 2022, a surrendered child is allowed a reconsideration period of
accepted.x: The Adoption Regulations, 2022 provide a two-month reconsideration period for surrendered children.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise reconsideration period from shorter and longer plausible intervals.

accepted.s: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 applies to
accepted.x: HAMA applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact personal-law group covered by the Act.
accepted.sec: Adoption - CARA, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, JJ Act route

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two principal legal routes of adoption?
o: HAMA applies to specified religious communities, whereas the JJ route is open to all religions
HAMA is open to all religions, whereas the JJ route is restricted to Hindus
Both HAMA and the JJ route are restricted to Hindus
Neither route permits adoption by persons belonging to different religions
accepted.x: HAMA applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, while the adoption route under the Juvenile Justice Act is open to all religions.
accepted.tq: Compare scope rather than confusing the two statutes because both concern adoption.
accepted.sec: Adoption - CARA, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, JJ Act route

accepted.x: Under Mission Vatsalya, CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories.

o: Outlay: Rs 10,916 crore; aftercare: Rs 40,000 per year for ages 14–18
Outlay: Rs 10,916 crore; aftercare: Rs 4,000 per month for ages 18–21
Outlay: Rs 1,916 crore; aftercare: Rs 400 per month
Outlay: Rs 91,016 crore; aftercare: Rs 4,000 per year for ages 18–25

o: SSA (2001) was followed by Samagra Shiksha (2018)
Teacher Education (2001) was followed by SSA (2018)

Samagra Shiksha, launched in 2018, merged which of the following schemes or components?
1. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
2. Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan
3. Teacher Education
Which of the statements given above are correct?

accepted.x: The allocation mentioned for Samagra Shiksha for 2026–27 is Rs 42,100 crore.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Samagra Shiksha is correct?
1. Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas are supported up to Class 12.
2. Support for Children with Special Needs is Rs 3,500.
3. The scheme merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: KGBVs are supported up to Class 12, CwSN support is Rs 3,500, and Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional coverage, financial support and scheme structure in one verification set.
accepted.sec: Universalisation of elementary education - SSA, Samagra Shiksha, no-detention changes

accepted.s: The RTE (Amendment) Act, 2019 changed the no-detention approach by
o: abolishing all re-examinations in elementary education
making automatic promotion compulsory up to Class 12
allowing examinations in Classes 5 and 8 and permitting holding back after failure in the re-examination
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment allowed examinations in Classes 5 and 8 and permitted a child to be held back after failing the re-examination.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise change to the no-detention policy and reject absolute formulations.
accepted.sec: Universalisation of elementary education - SSA, Samagra Shiksha, no-detention changes

accepted.s: According to the current assessment of implementation of the RTE quota under Section 12(1)(c), it has been effectively implemented in
accepted.x: The quota was reported to be effectively implemented in only 16 States and Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Use the word “only” as a cue to identify the limited implementation figure, not the total coverage figure.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court has described quality elementary teacher education as vital to the effective realisation of
accepted.x: The Supreme Court stressed that quality elementary teacher education is vital to Article 21A, the constitutional right to education.

accepted.s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, a child is defined as a person
o: below 14 years, without parental consent requirements
below 16 years, with consent of the school
below 18 years, requiring verifiable parental consent
below 21 years, requiring consent of the District Magistrate
accepted.x: The DPDP Act, 2023 defines a child as a person below 18 years and requires verifiable parental consent for processing the child's data.
accepted.tq: Compare the data-protection definition of child with the age thresholds under education and labour laws.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Operation Muskaan in Andhra Pradesh reportedly rescued over
accepted.x: Operation Muskaan rescued over 1,200 children from urban hubs in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Check both the scale and the target group rather than accepting a swapped number or beneficiary category.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court case Unni Krishnan (1993), relevant to the development of the right to education, arose from
accepted.x: The Unni Krishnan case of 1993 arose from Andhra Pradesh and is an important milestone in the development of the right to education.
accepted.tq: Recall the State origin of the landmark case instead of confusing it with its constitutional consequence.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the age thresholds under the three child-related legal frameworks?
o: POCSO: below 21; child labour law: below 16; RTE: 6–14 years
POCSO: below 14; child labour law: below 18; RTE: 6–18 years
POCSO: 6–14 years; child labour law: below 18; RTE: below 14 years
POCSO: below 18; child labour law: below 14; RTE: 6–14 years
accepted.x: POCSO defines a child as below 18 years, child labour law uses the below-14 threshold stated here, and RTE covers children aged 6–14 years.
accepted.tq: Place each age range with its correct statute before comparing the three frameworks.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The age of consent under POCSO has been a subject of criticism and debate.
2. The transfer system under the Juvenile Justice framework has been criticised as arbitrary.
3. Vacant seats under the RTE quota have also been identified as a concern.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are identified areas of criticism and debate: the age of consent, arbitrariness in the JJ transfer system and vacant RTE quota seats.
accepted.tq: Recognise a set of related criticisms without treating one policy concern as exclusive.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
